html:
In 1959 the Ethiopian Orthodox Church got its own patriarch for the first time. For some sixteen centuries it had been led by bishops sent from Egypt by the Coptic patriarch of Alexandria.

The tie went back to the 4th century, when Aksum became Christian and Frumentius was made its first bishop in Alexandria. Ever after, the head of the Ethiopian church, the abuna, was an Egyptian monk chosen by the Coptic Church. He often did not speak the local languages, and Ethiopian rulers had to send to Cairo for each new one.

In the 20th century Emperor Haile Selassie pressed for change. Ethiopian bishops were first consecrated in 1929. In 1951 Abuna Basilios became the first Ethiopian-born head of the church, and in 1959 the Coptic Pope Cyril VI raised him to patriarch, making the church self-governing.

The church stayed in communion with the Copts. Under the Derg it lost its lands and a patriarch was killed. After Eritrea's independence the Eritrean church broke away too, in 1993.
sum: In 1959 the Ethiopian Orthodox Church got its own patriarch for the first time. For some sixteen centuries it had been led by bishops sent from Egypt by the Coptic patriarch of Alexandria.
